# Deviations from Knope in ported fixtures

Each entry names a Knope fixture that cannot be ported unchanged, and why (spec: Testing strategy).

| Fixture | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validate/kitchen_sink` | Workflow names such as `Cannot SelectJiraIssue without Jira config ` must be renamed (no spaces, no trailing space). The Jira, GitHub issue and `SwitchBranches` workflows are in `validate/kitchen_sink_issues`, skipped until M11. | Remeris restricts workflow names to `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` because a `.` would break the koanf key path (spec F3.1). Knope allows any string. |
| Version grammar (F1.1) | `1.2.3-rc4`, `1.2.3-rc.4.5`, `1.2.3+build.7` and `1.2.3-alpha.beta.1` are valid versions. Knope rejected them, so tags like these were skipped; they now count as releases. | Full SemVer 2.0.0 (D8). |
| Version grammar (F1.1) | Rejected now, accepted by Knope: leading zeros (`01.2.3`, which Knope read as `1.2.3`, and `1.2.3-rc.01`) and a leading `+` on a number (`+1.2.3`, accepted by Rust's integer parser). Build identifiers may keep leading zeros. Numeric identifiers, pre-release ones included, must fit in a uint64; SemVer itself sets no limit. | Full SemVer 2.0.0 (D8), with the uint64 limit of spec F1.1. |
| Version ordering (F1.1) | Pre-releases are ordered by SemVer 2.0.0 section 11 precedence, not by "label string, then number". Both give the same order for the `label.N` shape. | Quirk Q2, D8. |
| Version display and equality (F1.1) | `+build` metadata is kept when a version is printed or written. Versions that differ only in build metadata have the same precedence but are not equal, so `1.2.3` and `1.2.3+b1` in one package are reported as inconsistent (F7.2). | D8. |
| `prepare_release/unknown_versioned_file_format` | The `Unknown file` help is `remeris identifies the type of file based on its name. Supported file names: …` instead of Knope's `Knope identities the type of file based on its name.` | Spec F2.2 asks the help to list the supported file names. |
| `versioned_files` with `deno.jsonc` | `deno.jsonc` is accepted as an explicit versioned file (DenoJson). Default detection still has no `deno.jsonc`, as in Knope. | Quirk Q11. |
| Regex versioned files (`{ path, regex }`) | Patterns use Go's RE2 syntax, not Rust's `regex` crate: `\d`, `\w`, `\s` and `\b` are ASCII-only, and Rust-only syntax such as `(?x)`, class set operations and `\u{…}` is an invalid pattern. Ordinary patterns like `\d+\.\d+\.\d+` behave the same. The `Invalid regex pattern` message carries Go's error text. | No Rust regex engine in Go; spec 0.3 picks stdlib `regexp`. |
| `Cargo.toml` edits | The whitespace around an edited value and a trailing comment on its line are kept: `version="1"   # note` becomes `version="3.0.0"   # note`. Knope's toml_edit resets the value's decor, so it writes `version= "3.0.0"` and drops the comment. CRLF line endings are kept too (new lines use the document's line ending); Knope rewrites the file with LF. | Format-preserving edits (spec F6.2): change only the bytes of the value. |
| `Cargo.toml` dependency edits | When `[workspace]` has no `dependencies` table, editing a dependency does not add `dependencies = {}` to `[workspace]`. Knope does, as a side effect of `entry().or_insert`. | The side effect is an accident of toml_edit's API, not a feature. |
| `pyproject.toml` with both `tool.poetry.version` and `project.version`, `[tool.poetry]` first | When the new version has a different length, Knope reuses stale byte offsets for the second replacement: a longer version writes a broken file (`version 10.20.300.0"`), a shorter one panics (`range end index … out of range`). Remeris writes both versions correctly. | Knope bug; spans are recomputed after each edit. |
| `pyproject.toml` with a multi-line string version (`version = """1.0.0"""`) | The delimiters are kept. Knope's span arithmetic rewrites it as `"1.0.1"`. | Knope bug. |
| `pyproject.toml` invalid or ill-typed content | The message keeps Knope's form `Could not deserialize {path} as a pyproject.toml: {err}`, but `{err}` is Go's TOML parser text, not serde's. | Different TOML library. |
| `package.json` with a duplicated top-level `version` key | The last value wins. Knope rejects the file (`duplicate field \`version\``); other duplicated keys keep the last value in both. | The JSON tree keeps the last value for every duplicated key, like serde_json's map; only Knope's struct deserializer treats `version` specially. |
| `[packages]` with no packages | An empty `[packages]` table is always an error (`The \`packages\` key is defined but does not contain any packages`). Knope reports it only when `[package]` is also defined; otherwise it falls back to package discovery. | Spec F2.2. |
| Read and write errors (`Error reading from {path}`, `Error writing to {path}`) | The cause is Go's OS error text (`is a directory`, `no such file or directory`), not Rust's (`Is a directory (os error 21)`). | Different standard library. |
| `prepare_release/invalid_versioned_files_package_json` | Expects `Error deserializing package.json: EOF`, where Knope prints `EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0`. | Different JSON library. |
| `bump_version/*` with `package.json` | The real run checks `git diff` of `package.json` instead of `cmp` against `out/package.json`. | The output has no final newline (Q10) and a txtar file always ends with one. |
| `bump_version/multiple_packages/release` | The ported `dryrun_stdout.log` expects `Cargo.toml: version = 0.1.3` (and the same for `package.json`); Knope's file has no `version = ` prefix. | The fixture is stale upstream: `multiple_packages/mod.rs` has no `mod release;`, so Knope never runs it. Knope's code writes the prefix, as in every other fixture. |
| Usage text with backticks (`--override-version`: ``Override the version set by `BumpVersion` or `PrepareRelease` …``) | The backticks are left out: `Override the version set by BumpVersion or PrepareRelease for the package.` | urfave/cli turns a backticked word into the flag's placeholder. |
| Package discovery errors | A discovery error (an unreadable workspace manifest, a bad glob, ...) is raised only by a workflow that reads the packages: one with a `PrepareRelease`, `BumpVersion`, `Release` or `CreateChangeFile` step, or a `Command` or `CreatePullRequest` that uses the `Version` or `ChangelogEntry` variable; and by `--validate` and `--generate`. `--help` and the other workflows, such as one with only a plain `Command`, run as usual. Knope reports it while loading the configuration, for every command. | A broken manifest must not stop a workflow that does not need the packages (spec F20.1). |
| `prepare_release/allow_empty` | The real run checks git's output line with the regular expression `^\[main [0-9a-f]+\] chore: prepare release 1\.0\.0$` instead of `cmp` against a `stdout.log` that has Knope's `[..]` wildcard. | `cmp` has no wildcard, and the commit hash changes at every run. |
| `--override-version` with a bad value | The error is our semver parse error (`Found invalid semantic version …`), not clap's `invalid value '…' for '--override-version <…>': …` wrapper. | urfave/cli has no per-value parser error of clap's form. |
| `--override-version` repeated with one package | The error text is `the argument '--override-version <OVERRIDE_ONE_VERSION>' cannot be used multiple times`, written by hand, without clap's usage lines and `For more information, try '--help'`. | urfave/cli accepts a repeated slice flag; remeris rejects it after package loading. |
| `--override-version` bad values | They are reported after the packages are loaded, with exit code 1. clap reports them first, with exit code 2. | The values are parsed once the packages are known (spec F3.1). |
| `prepare_release/*`, `git_release/*`, `default_workflows/*` | `[DATE]` is the fixed date `2026-01-01`, set with `env REMERIS_FAKE_DATE=2026-01-01`, which only the test hook in `cmd/remeris/main_test.go` reads (the binary does not). A dry run's output is compared through `rstrip`, which removes the space that ends `Would add the following to {path}: `. | Scripts need a fixed date, and the repository's whitespace check rejects trailing spaces in a script. |
| `prepare_release/*` and `git_release/multiple_packages` with `package.json` | The real run checks the version with `grep` instead of `cmp` against `out/package.json`; input files that had no final newline get one. | Q10: the output has no final newline and a txtar file always ends with one. |
| `prepare_release/changesets/invalid_change_file` | The errors are the message and help lines as rendered by `internal/diag`, without miette's graphics and `changesets::could_not_read_changeset` code line. | Spec F3.3, D4. |
| `prepare_release/enable_prerelease`, `override_prerelease_label` | One script per case (`_with_option`, `_with_env`); two more cover `REMERIS_PRERELEASE_LABEL` and the flag beating the environment. The environment variable of the ported ones is still `KNOPE_PRERELEASE_LABEL`. | D1: `REMERIS_*` is read first. |
| `prepare_release/*`, `git_release/*`, `default_workflows/*` git setup | Commits are made with `exec git commit --allow-empty --author 'Knope <knope@example.com>'`, and no file is added to the index before the run, as in Knope's harness. | Same as Knope's `TestCase`; recorded because `git add` of untracked files is part of what the real run does. |
| `--prerelease-label=` (empty) | An empty value counts as no flag: the step's own `prerelease_label`, if any, applies, otherwise the release is stable. Knope uses the empty label and produces the invalid version `1.1.0-.0`. | An empty label cannot make a valid SemVer pre-release. |
| `--verbose` output of PrepareRelease | The debug lines are not matched: remeris logs `Determining new version for default` for an unnamed package and the rule implied by each change even with `--override-version`, and does not log `Only checking commits with scopes`, `Using {RULE} rule to bump from` or `Pre-release label … selected`. | Debug output is not part of the compatibility contract; no fixture checks it. |
| Git errors outside a repository or with no commits | The cause is the `git` command's message (`fatal: not a git repository …`, `fatal: bad revision 'HEAD'`), not libgit2's (`could not find repository at '.'`, `reference 'refs/heads/main' not found`). The message, help and exit code match. | remeris runs the `git` CLI (spec F9). |
| `prepare_release/inconsistent_versions` | The error is the message and help lines as rendered by `internal/diag`, without miette's graphics, code line and wrapping. The dry run and the real run share one `stderr.log`. | Spec F3.3, D4. |
| `prepare_release/verbose` | `Running step PrepareRelease {PrereleaseLabel: AllowEmpty:false IgnoreConventionalCommits:false}` replaces Rust's `Debug` form. The script is skipped until the missing debug lines (`{file} has version {v}`, `Looking for Git tags matching package name.`, `Only checking commits with scopes`, `Using {RULE} rule to bump from`, `Rule is MAJOR, but major component is 0`) are printed. | Spec F3.2 ("debug repr"). |
| `prepare_release/*` and `git_release/*` with `[..]` (commit hashes) | `cmp` is replaced by `rstrip` and an anchored `grep` regex, or by an anchored `stdout` regex (`(?m)`), in which `[..]` becomes `[0-9a-f]+`. | `cmp` has no wildcards. |
| `prepare_release/go_modules_major_versions_v2` | The input `CHANGELOG.md` keeps its literal `[DATE]` for the old `1.1.0` heading; only the new heading has `2026-01-01`. | Knope redacts only its own output. |
| `prepare_release/deno_workspaces` | The trailing space after `"name": "@scope/second-package",` in the input is removed. | The repository's whitespace check. |
| `prepare_release/*` with multi-paragraph commits and merges | `Commit("a\n\nb")` becomes `git commit -m a -m b`; branches and merges use `git switch -c` and `git merge --no-ff --no-edit`; Knope's `sleep(1)` becomes `exec sleep 1`. | A txtar command line cannot hold a newline. |
| `prepare_release/*` and `default_workflows/*` with files Knope lists unchanged in `out/` | `cp X X.orig` before the run and `cmp X X.orig` after it. | txtar has no separate expected directory. |
| `prepare_release/*` with JSON outputs | Where Knope's `out/*.json` has no final newline, the script compares against `printf %s "$(cat out/X)"`. All such files are in skipped scripts (tauri, npm). `prepare_release/deno_*` compare the `deno.json` files with `cmp` against `out/`, which keep the final newline (see deno.json below). | Q10: txtar cannot express a missing final newline. |
| `default_workflows/get_version/multi_package` | `stderr.log` is `Error: No workflow named get-version` instead of clap's `error: unrecognized subcommand 'get-version'` with its usage lines. | remeris reports an unknown workflow in its own words (`cli/no_workflow`); the CLI is urfave/cli, not clap, so clap's texts and layout are not reproduced (spec F3.1). |
| Ported scripts with `expected_tags` | Knope compares the sorted `git tag --contains HEAD`; the scripts run that command and `cmp` it with `tags.txt`. | Same check, written as a testscript command. |
| `prepare_release/no_version_change` | The error is the message and help lines as rendered by `internal/diag`, without miette's graphics, `releases::no_release` code line and wrapping. | Spec F3.3, D4. |
| `prepare_release/go_modules_*` | `go.mod` inputs and outputs end with a newline; Knope's files have none. | A txtar file always ends with a newline; remeris keeps the newline it read (as Q10 for JSON). |
| Log line of a step without fields (`--verbose`) | `Running step Release`, as Knope prints a unit variant. Steps with fields keep the Go form (`prepare_release/verbose`). | Spec F3.2. |
| Credentials (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN`) | An empty environment variable counts as unset, so the stored token or the prompt is used. Knope uses the empty string as the token. | An empty token never authenticates; falling through is friendlier (spec F15.2). |
| Credentials directory | Credentials are read from `<config>/remeris/`. A value found only in `<config>/knope/` is used and copied into the remeris directory; if the copy fails, the value is still used and the failure is logged at debug level. Knope has one directory. | Rename to remeris (D1) without asking existing Knope users again. |
| `github_release/*` | `[COMMIT]` is matched as 40 hex digits by an anchored `grep` on the output after `rstrip`, as for the other commit hashes. `[DATE]` is `2026-01-01`, also in the input changelogs of `release_assets_*` and `no_previous_tag`, where Knope's input holds the literal `[DATE]`. A final `git tag --list` check shows that the dry run made no tag. | `cmp` has no wildcards; scripts need a fixed date. |
| `prepare_release/changelog_header_level_detection` | No longer skipped: the GitHub release line it expects is printed since M7. The commit is matched as 40 hex digits. | Same as above. |
| Pull request lookup (`$pr_number`, `$pr_author_login`) | The request goes through go-github, which sets its own `X-GitHub-Api-Version`; Knope sends `2026-03-10`. | The client library owns that header (spec F16.4). |
| `create_pull_requests/*` (Quirk Q3) | The dry run prints `Would create or update a pull request from main to main:`; Knope prints `refs/heads/main` because its `current_branch` returns the full ref. A real run sends `head=owner:main` and `"head": "main"` (Knope: `refs/heads/main`). Branches with a `/` keep it (`feature/x`). | Spec F18, Q3: Knope's value is a bug; the short name is what GitHub expects. |
| Gitea `CreatePullRequest` lookup | The open pull requests are listed with `state=open&base_branch={base}&limit=50&page={n}` (at most 20 pages) and filtered on the client: head branch, head repository owner (case-insensitive) and base branch must match. Knope sends `state=open&head=owner:branch&base=base` and updates the first result. | Gitea's list endpoint has no `head` filter, so Knope's request returns every open pull request and it may update an unrelated one (spec F17, F18). |
| Gitea `CreatePullRequest` branch (Quirk Q3) | The dry run, the lookup and the `head` of the new pull request use the full short branch name (`feature/x`). Knope uses the last path segment of the ref (`x`). | Spec F18, Q3: the last segment is wrong for branches with a `/`. |
| `create_pull_requests/gitea_*`, `github_and_gitea` | Our own dry-run scripts: Knope has no Gitea fixture. With both forges the three lines are printed once per forge, as in Knope. | Coverage for M8. |
| Forge detection (F20.6) | A remote with a single `/`-less part such as `git@github.com:r.git` gives no GitHub. Knope computes `parts.len() - 2` on a `usize` there: that panics in a debug build and wraps to "no owner" in a release build, so the release behaviour is kept. Other quirks stay: `https://github.com/r` gives owner `github.com`, and a trailing slash gives an empty repo. | Spec F20.6; the debug panic is not a behaviour to copy. |
| Gitea detection (F17, F20.6): known host | Gitea is detected only when the parsed host of the first remote equals a known public host (`codeberg.org`, case-insensitive, no port). Knope tests `remote.contains("codeberg.org")`, so `https://evil.example/codeberg.org/r` and `https://codeberg.org.evil.example/o/r` give Gitea there. GitHub is checked first and Gitea only when GitHub is not detected (Knope can set both). | A substring match would send the release request, and the token, to a host the remote only mentions. |
| Gitea detection (F17, F20.6): userinfo | The userinfo of the remote is dropped: `https://user:token@codeberg.org/o/r` and `ssh://git@codeberg.org/o/r` give host `https://codeberg.org`. Knope keeps it (`https://user:token@codeberg.org`). | A credential must never reach the configuration, a log line or a request. Other `try_from_remote` behaviour is kept: `http` is forced to `https`, `https://h/o/r/x` gives repo `r/x`, a trailing slash stays in the repo. |
| Forge detection from a subdirectory (no `knope.toml`) | The first remote is read from the repository that contains the working directory, as for every other Git access of remeris. Knope opens `.` only and finds no remote below the repository root. | The Git backends discover the repository upward (spec F9.0); package discovery from a subdirectory usually finds no package anyway. |
| Gitea authentication (`[gitea]` forge) | The token is sent in the header `Authorization: token {token}`. Knope sends it as the `access_token` query parameter. | A token in a URL ends up in logs, proxies and error messages (spec F17, decision). |
| Gitea `host` | The host must have a scheme (`remeris::gitea::invalid_host` on a real run; a dry run prints it as written), use https (http only for loopback hosts), have no userinfo, query, fragment, space or control character, and trailing slashes are trimmed when URLs are built (`https://x/gitea/` and `https://x/gitea` both reach `https://x/gitea/api/v1/…`). A redirect to another host or port, or from https to http, is refused, and `Authorization` is never sent to another origin. Knope accepts any string and follows redirects with the token in the URL. The token is also replaced by `[REDACTED]` in every Gitea error message. | The `host` of a repository's configuration must not make the token leave the instance (spec F17, decision). |
| Jira authentication | `Authorization: Basic base64(email:jira_token)` is added by a transport that only the origin of the `[jira]` url reaches, under the retry policy; the email is asked before the token, both once per run (stored answers are kept). The token and the Basic blob (standard, URL-safe, padded or not) are replaced by `[REDACTED]`, also URL-escaped in upper or lower case, in every Jira error; the email is not redacted, and the log says only `Using the Jira token`. Knope builds the header by hand for every request. There is no environment variable for the email or the token, as in Knope. | Same hardening as Gitea (spec F15, F17). |
| Jira `url` | Checked like the Gitea `host`: a scheme is required (`remeris::jira::invalid_url` on a real run; a dry run prints it as written), https unless loopback (`remeris::jira::insecure_url`), no userinfo, query, fragment, space or control character, trailing slashes trimmed, a context path allowed. A redirect to another host or port, or from https to http, is refused (`remeris::jira::redirect`). Knope accepts any string and follows redirects with the header. | The url must not make the credential leave the site. |
| Jira HTTP status | Every response status is checked: a 4xx, 5xx or other non-2xx answer is `Problem communicating with Jira while {activity}: HTTP status client error (401 Unauthorized) for url (…) with body: …` (the body is scrubbed, then cut at 2 KiB on a character boundary; 401 and 403 add a help). The transition `POST` is sent once and never retried (a 5xx or a dropped connection is reported), where reads and the search are retried like every request. Knope reads the body of any answer as JSON and ignores the status of the transition request, so a failed transition looks like a success. A response over 32 MiB is refused. | A wrong credential or a failed transition must be reported. |
| Jira JQL and issue key | The status and the project are quoted in the JQL (`status = "In Progress" AND project = "PRJ"`) with `\` and `"` escaped; Knope pastes them unquoted. One pair of matching outer quotes (`'` or `"`) is removed first, so a configuration written for Knope (`status = "'In Progress'"`) gives the same query. The issue key is escaped as one path segment (`PRJ-1/../x` cannot reach another endpoint) and an empty key, `.` and `..` are refused (`remeris::jira::invalid_issue_key`). The search is `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with `maxResults` 50 (D5). | Values from the configuration or from Jira must not change the query or the endpoint. |
| Gitea release response | Any valid JSON is accepted as the answer to `POST .../releases`. Knope requires an object with `url` and `upload_url` and fails with `Trouble decoding the response from Gitea while creating a release` otherwise. Invalid JSON, or an empty body, is still that error. | Older Gitea versions send no `upload_url`, and remeris does not use the response (spec F16.2). |
| Gitea dry run (`gitea_release/*`, `multi_forge_release/*`, `default_workflows/release/gitea`) | The host in `Would create a release on Gitea [{host}]` is printed as written, except that a user name and password are removed (`https://user:pw@gitea.example.com` prints as `https://gitea.example.com`); a host with `@` that cannot be parsed prints `[REDACTED]`. The fixtures use `https://codeberg.org`, so their output is Knope's. | A dry run does not check the host, and a password in it must not reach a terminal or a log (spec F17). |
| `deno.lock` reading (`pkg/versioning/internal/denolock`): arrays as structs | A JSON array where deno_lockfile reads a struct (an `npm` or `jsr` entry, a workspace member, a link, `packageJson`) is an error (`invalid type: sequence, expected struct …`). The Rust serde derives accept an array there and read it positionally. | No lockfile written by Deno has that shape; guessing positional fields would only hide a corrupt file. |
| `deno.lock` reading: non-ASCII npm ids | An npm package id or dependency that starts with a multibyte character is read normally. In Rust `extract_nv_from_id` slices `value[1..]`, which panics, so Knope crashes in `write()`. | A panic is not a behaviour to copy; for every other input the results are the same. |
| `deno.lock` printing: floats | A float in free-form JSON (`packageJson.overrides`, `peerDependenciesMeta`) prints in the `1e+16`, `1e-7`, `1000.0` style shared with `jsonedit`. This assumes the number formatter of the `serde_json` that Knope is built with, and has not been checked against the version Knope pins. | Integers, strings and the rest of the file are exact; floats do not occur in lockfiles written by Deno. |
| `internal/glob`: symbolic links to directories below `**` | A directory is not entered again while one of its ancestors in the walk is the same directory (`x -> .`, `a/b -> ..`): the link can match, its content is not walked. A link to any other directory is still followed, once per path, as in the crate. Without file identity (a file system that is not os-backed) a chain of more than 64 links is not entered. A walk that reads more than 1,000,000 directories stops with `glob: too many directories` and the matches found so far. The crate and Knope follow such links until the operating system says `ELOOP` (about 2^40 paths for two links to `.`). Results are the same for trees without a loop. | The repository is untrusted (npm `workspaces`, release `assets`, Deno members): a hostile layout must not hang the release. |
| `internal/glob`: patterns | A NUL byte, or a length over 4096 bytes, is an error (`glob: NUL byte in pattern …`, `glob: pattern too long …`). Matching is polynomial (O(pattern x name)), not exponential in the number of stars as in the first port; the answers are the crate's. | Hostile patterns from the same source. |
| `internal/glob`: repeated `**` | Each (path, pattern component) pair is expanded once, so `**/a/**/a/…/x` over a deep tree is polynomial instead of C(depth, k). A path the crate lists more than once (for example `a/a/a` for `**/a/**/a`) is listed once, at its first place; the order of the others is unchanged. | Hostile trees and patterns from the same source. |
| `internal/glob`: symbolic links | As in the crate, links are followed, including links that leave the root: with `os.DirFS`, `**` can match files outside the checkout, so a release `assets` glob can name a file outside the repository. Callers decide whether to accept that. A walk that reads too many directories returns `glob: too many directories (more than 1000000) while expanding "…"; use a more specific pattern` and no matches. | Parity with the crate; the limit is the safety net. |

## M9 versioned files

Each format's pull request edits only its own section. Rows follow the table above: what differs from Knope and why.

### Cargo.lock

| Knope | remeris | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edits the `toml_edit` document and prints it back. | Splices the bytes of the `version` value (or appends `version = "..."` to the table), so everything else is untouched, as for Cargo.toml. | Same output as `toml_edit` for the files Cargo writes; byte-exact for hand-edited ones. |
| A trailing comment on the edited `version` line is dropped (the decor reset of `value(...)`). | The comment is kept. | Same family as the Cargo.toml rows. |
| `to_string()` ends the last pair with a newline. | A missing final newline is kept as read. | Byte-level splice. |
| The unsupported-version warning prints the `toml_edit` item with its decor. | The same text is built from the file's bytes: the whitespace after `=`, the raw value, then the rest of the line (whitespace and comment), so `version = 5` warns `Unsupported version of Cargo.lock:  5. Outcome may be unexpected` (two spaces). | Not confirmed byte for byte against a Knope run (no fixture shows it); the trailing-comment rendering (`Cargo.lock:  5 # c.`) is derived from toml_edit's decor rules and could not be confirmed against Knope. A top-level `[version]` table prints an empty value. |
| Error help says "Knope may not yet support a newer format". | "remeris may not yet support a newer format". | Naming (D1). |

### gleam.toml

| Knope | remeris | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edits the `toml_edit` document and prints it back. | Splices the bytes of the `version` value, or inserts `version = "..."` after the last top-level pair when it is missing (unreachable after F7.2 validation). | Same as Cargo.toml. |

### package-lock.json

| Case | Deviation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepare_release/npm_{package,dependencies}` | The real run checks the lock file and `package.json` against `printf %s "$(cat out/X)"` instead of `cmp` against `out/X`. | Q10: the output has no final newline and a txtar file always ends with one. |
| An invalid JSON document | The message after `Error deserializing {path}: ` is the text of the Go JSON error, not serde_json's. | Different JSON library. |
| `package-lock.json` with a duplicated key | The last value wins, in the position of the first. | The JSON tree behaves like serde_json's map. |

The rest is Knope's behaviour on purpose, quirks included: a dependency edit always rewrites the file and adds its diff,
even when nothing matches or `packages` is missing; only entries of `packages` with a `name` field are matched (npm v7
entries such as `node_modules/x` have none, and the legacy `dependencies` section is not touched); a matching
`dependencies` or `devDependencies` member is replaced by the bare version whatever it held, so a leading `^` is lost;
the `lockfileVersion` warning appears on every edit and also for a missing or float (`3.0`) value.

### tauri.conf.json

| Case | Deviation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepare_release/tauri_conf_json` | The real run checks the Tauri files and `package.json` against `printf %s "$(cat out/X)"` instead of `cmp` against `out/X`. | Q10: the output has no final newline and a txtar file always ends with one. |
| An invalid JSON document | The message after `Error deserializing {path}: ` is the text of the Go JSON error, not serde_json's. | Different JSON library. |
| `tauri.conf.json` with a duplicated top level `version` key | The last value wins, in the position of the first. Knope rejects the file at load time (`duplicate field \`version\``). Other duplicated keys keep the last value in both. | Knope reads the version through a derived struct, which refuses a repeated field; the JSON tree keeps the last value like serde_json's map. |

The rest is Knope's behaviour on purpose: Tauri v2's `"version": "../package.json"` is rejected as not a version, the help
text names `tauri.conf.json` for the platform variants too, the diff is the bare version, and `.json5` and `Tauri.toml`
are not supported.

### pubspec.yaml

| Case | Deviation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any edit | Only the bytes of the top-level `version` scalar are replaced, found from the position yaml.v3 reports for the key's value. A trailing `# comment`, the quote style (`'1.0.0'`, `"1.0.0"`) and every other byte stay. Knope replaces the whole line and drops the comment and the quotes. | Knope's `raw.replace(line, ...)` is a text edit that loses formatting. |
| A nested `  version: 1.0.0` (or the same text under another key) | Left alone, also when it comes before the top-level key. Knope's `replace` rewrites every occurrence of the line text in the file. | Knope's edit hits unrelated keys. |
| A BOM at the start of the file, or CRLF, tabs and multi-byte characters before the version | Handled: the BOM is skipped and line endings are kept. Knope's `starts_with("version: ")` finds no line behind a BOM and then re-serialises the whole file. | Knope's search is a byte-prefix test on the line. |
| `version: >-` / `\|` block scalars, anchors (`&v`), tags (`!!str`), a double-quoted value with escapes, a quoted value over several lines | `remeris` fails with `Could not update {path}: ...` (`remeris::pubspec_yaml::serialize`) and does not write. Knope rewrites the line (breaking the block scalar). | The scalar's source is not the simple text the splice replaces. |
| `version: *alias` | The load fails with ``YAML `version` field was not a string``. | An alias node is not a string scalar; the YAML is never expanded. |
| A flow mapping at the top level (`{version: 1.0.0}`) | Spliced like a block mapping. Knope finds no `version: ` line and re-serialises it in block style. | Same splice. |
| Flutter versions such as `1.0.0+1` | The build metadata is part of the version (D8), so `1.0.0+1` loads. A bump writes the new version as semver prints it: the old `+1` is not carried over, and build metadata on the new version is kept. Nothing is special-cased. | No Flutter rule in the spec. |
| Two top-level `version` keys | The load fails with ``YAML contained more than one top-level `version` field``. | Knope's choice between them is the YAML library's. |
| An invalid YAML document | The message after `Error deserializing {path}: ` is the text of the go-yaml error, not saphyr's. | Different YAML library. |
| A plain value shaped like a timestamp (`version: 2001-01-01`) | The load fails with ``YAML `version` field was not a string``, because yaml.v3 tags it `!!timestamp`. Knope reads it as a string and fails with a semver parse error. | Different YAML library and tag resolution. |
| The help text of the `Could not update {path}: ...` error | It says to write `version: x.y.z` on one line without an anchor or a tag. Knope's serialize help says to report a bug. | remeris refuses to edit such a file instead of re-serialising it. |
| Spec F6.2 ("replace that line only", re-serialise when no line) | remeris splices the scalar's bytes only, in the first top-level `version` key, and appends a line for the unreachable no-key case. It never re-serialises. | See the first rows. |
| A file without a top-level `version` | Never reached: the load fails first (as in Knope). The insert branch appends `version: {v}` on a new line at the end of a block mapping, with the file's line ending, instead of re-serialising the document. | The spec's re-serialise branch is unreachable after F7.2 validation. |

The rest is Knope's behaviour: exactly one YAML document that is a mapping, a top-level `version` that is a string (`version: 1.0`
is a float and fails), the diff is the bare version, and a dependency is ignored.

### pom.xml

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any `pom.xml` edit (Quirk Q7) | Only the content of the first direct-child `<version>` of `<project>` is replaced, as plain text. The XML declaration, comments, indentation, line endings, byte order mark, attribute quoting, entities and everything else stay byte for byte. Knope parses the file and writes the tree again: it drops the declaration and the comments, re-indents with two spaces and writes LF. Knope's `bump_version/maven` fixture is unchanged because its input already has Knope's layout. | Spec F6.2, Quirk Q7: better behaviour, a smaller diff in the user's repository. |
| `<version>` that holds entities, a CDATA section or comments | The whole inner range is replaced by the new version. | The element text is replaced, not its parts. |
| Self-closing `<version/>` | `Version()` fails (no text), so a bump stops with the missing-property error before any edit. `SetVersion` itself turns it into `<version>v</version>`. | The element has no content to replace. |
| `<version>` missing | `Version()` fails, as in Knope. `SetVersion` inserts `<version>` after the `</artifactId>` that is a direct child of `<project>`, with that line's indentation and line ending, or else before `</project>`. Knope inserts into the tree and re-emits it. | Same placement rule as Knope, byte-exact edit. |
| Encodings | UTF-8 (with or without a byte order mark), ISO-8859-1 and US-ASCII declarations are read. Any other declared encoding, and UTF-16, is the error `Unsupported XML encoding {name} in {path}` (`remeris::maven_pom::encoding`). In an ISO-8859-1 or US-ASCII file, bytes of 0x80 and above are read as placeholders so that byte offsets stay exact; a `<version>` whose text holds such a byte is read from the original bytes and fails as a non-version, and a US-ASCII file with bytes of 0x80 and above is accepted rather than rejected. | A surgical edit needs byte offsets into the original bytes; converting other encodings would change them and the written file. |
| Invalid XML | The message keeps Knope's form `Invalid XML in {path}: {err}`, but `{err}` is the text of Go's `encoding/xml`, not xml-rs. Files that xml-rs rejects and Go accepts (or the reverse) differ in edge cases; Go also rejects an XML declaration whose version is not `1.0`. Text or a second root element after the root is rejected, as in Knope. | Different XML library (spec 0.3). |
| Whitespace in `<version>` | The text is not trimmed, as in Knope: ` 1.2.3` is not a version. Text that is only white space counts as missing, as in Knope (xml-rs drops white-space-only runs). | Parity. |
| Whitespace-only run split by a comment | `<version>1.2.3<!--c--> </version>` and `<version> <!--c-->1.2.3</version>` read as `1.2.3`. xml-rs may yield the space as text, and Knope would then reject it (unverified). | Remeris drops every whitespace-only text token. |
| Blank CDATA or `&#32;` | `<version><![CDATA[ ]]></version>` and `<version>&#32;</version>` report the missing-property error. Knope gives a semver error (unverified). | Whitespace-only text tokens are dropped, whatever their form. |
| Undeclared namespace prefix | `<foo:version>` without `xmlns:foo` is accepted. xml-rs rejects it. | encoding/xml does not check prefixes. |
| Encoding pseudo-attribute | Remeris looks for the declaration only at offset 0 (after a BOM); Go's decoder honours it anywhere. Safe but inconsistent. | Detection is a small byte scan. |
| Insertion placement (missing `<version>`, unreachable after F7.2) | A trailing comment after `</artifactId>` moves down after the new element; the indentation is that of `</project>` plus one level; a single-line project gets a lone newline before the element. | Minimal rule, not polished. |
| `dependency` on pom.xml | Knope ignores it in `set_version` and rejects it when the package is configured (package.rs). Remeris rejects it at configuration time too (`validateDependency`, `Format.SupportsDependency`), and `SetVersion` also returns `UnsupportedDependency` as a guard. | Same outcome, earlier guard. |

### deno.json and deno.jsonc

| Case | Deviation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any edit (Quirk Q6) | Only the bytes of the top level `version` value are replaced. Comments, trailing commas, key order, indentation, line endings, a byte order mark and everything else stay. Knope sets the value in the parsed tree and prints it again as plain pretty JSON, which drops the comments. | Spec F6.2, Q6: what the Deno documentation promises. |
| Final newline | The output keeps the final newline of the input (or its absence). Knope never writes one (Q10). The `out` files of the fixtures copied to `pkg/versioning/versionedfile/testdata/deno_json/` have a final newline added; `prepare_release/deno_*` compare the output with `cmp` directly, without the `printf %s "$(cat …)"` step. | Byte-level splice; a txtar file always ends with a newline. |
| Duplicate top level `version` | The last member is read and patched, like jsonc-parser's last-wins. Earlier ones are left as they are. | Same value as Knope reads. |
| Setting the version the file already has | The file is not changed, even if the value is written with escapes (`"1\u002e0.0"`). | Identity. |
| `version` missing | `Version()` fails with `This file can't contain a version`, as in Knope. `SetVersion` adds `"version": "{v}"` as the last member, with the indentation and line ending of the previous member and a trailing comma if the object had one; a line comment ending the previous member's line stays there. Knope inserts into the tree and prints it again. | Unreachable after the F7.2 validation. |
| Root that is not an object | `Version()` fails (no version). `SetVersion` fails with `Could not update {path}: the top level value is not a JSON object`. Knope writes the file again unchanged apart from the formatting, and records the diff. | Nothing to patch; unreachable after validation. |
| Syntax accepted by jsonc-parser only | Single-quoted strings, unquoted keys, hexadecimal numbers and a leading `+` are rejected (`Could not parse {path}: hujson: line L, column C: ...`). Knope accepts them. | hujson implements JWCC (JSON with comments and trailing commas), which is stricter. |
| Empty file, or only comments | `Could not parse {path}: ...`. Knope reads it as `null` (no version). | hujson requires a value. |
| Parse error text | `Could not parse {path}: {err}` with the text of hujson's error, not jsonc-parser's. | Different library. |
| Content after the root value | Rejected (`invalid character ... after top-level value`). | hujson. |
| Nesting depth (remeris addition) | Objects and arrays nested deeper than 10000 levels are a parse error (`Could not parse {path}: nesting is deeper than 10000 levels`). Brackets inside strings and comments do not count. Knope has no such limit (jsonc-parser reports its own depth error). | hujson recurses without a limit: a few megabytes of `[` would overflow the stack, which Go cannot recover from. |
| `dependency` | Ignored, with no diff and no write, as in Knope. | `deno.lock` owns dependency versions. |

A line comment cannot contain U+2028 or U+2029 (hujson rejects them).

### deno.lock

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A lockfile that deno_lockfile's `from_json` rejects, edited by a `SetVersion` that matches a specifier | Error `Could not update {path}: {reason}` (`remeris::deno_lock::update`), where `{reason}` is the text of the model error, for example `Invalid redirects section: invalid type: integer `5`, expected a map`. Knope's `write()` ends in `from_json(self.json).ok()?`, so it writes nothing and prints nothing: the release goes on and the lockfile is silently left behind. | A release that leaves the lockfile out of date without a word is worse than a clear failure. The check runs in `SetVersion`, after the match, so a lockfile that no edit touches is never rejected (as in Knope). |
| When a write happens | Same as Knope: only when at least one `specifiers` entry named the dependency (and had a string value). Then the whole file is re-printed in the canonical form of deno_lockfile (2-space indent, fixed key order, sorted maps, final newline, empty sections and unknown top-level keys dropped), not patched in place. A call with no dependency, no `specifiers` object or no match changes nothing. | Parity; the canonical print is what Deno itself writes. |
| Specifier keys | The key text is not rewritten, only its value; the printed key is the normalised requirement (`^1.0.0` prints as `1`), a property of the printer. | Parity with Knope's `deno_lock.rs`. |
| JSON syntax errors | `Error deserializing {path}: {err}` with the text of Go's JSON reader, not serde_json's. | Different JSON library. |
| `Version()` | Always `This file can't contain a version`, as in Knope (code `remeris::versioned_file::no_version`). | Parity. |
| Removing a renamed key | Like serde_json with `preserve_order` (`Map::remove` is a swap remove), the last member fills the hole and the renamed entry is inserted at the end (an insert over an existing key replaces its value in place). It only shows for `jsr` keys that differ by build metadata alone, which the model treats as one key: the last one in the object wins. | Parity, kept on purpose. |
| Malformed shapes (rewrite side) | The rewrite walks the JSON tree and ignores a section, member or list of the wrong type (an array where an object is expected, a non-string list item) without failing; the model then decides. A shape the model rejects (`"workspace": []`, a member or link that is an array, `"jsr": []`, an npm id without a version) is the `Could not update` error above; a `specifiers` that is not an object is a no-op. Multibyte package names and ids work (`é@1.0.0` is renamed like any other); the Rust slicing that panics on a non-ASCII id is not reproduced. | Same rule as the from_json deviation: no silent skip. The reader side is recorded with the denolock model. |
| Cost | Each `SetVersion` that matches deep-clones the JSON tree, edits the copy, and runs `FromJSON` and `Print` on it (about 2-3 copies of the lockfile in memory at once, for example around 150 MB for a 50 MB lockfile; all work is linear in its size). Knope edits the tree it owns and builds the model once, at write time. | The files are immutable values (F6.1), and the model is checked early to report the failure. |

## M10 package discovery

### Cargo workspaces

| Knope | remeris | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root `Cargo.toml` that does not parse: `Could not parse TOML in Cargo.toml: …` with `toml_edit`'s text. | Same message and code (`remeris::workspace::toml`), with Go's TOML library error after the colon. A missing file, or a valid one without `workspace.members`, is no error. | A different TOML library. |
| Member that cannot be read or parsed. | `Could not parse TOML in {member}/Cargo.toml: …` has Go's TOML text. An unreadable member is `Error reading from {member}/Cargo.toml: …` (code `remeris::fs::read`) with the Go file system's cause (`file does not exist`, `not a regular file`), where Knope has the operating system's text (`No such file or directory (os error 2)`). | Different libraries. |
| Manifest of any size is read whole. | A manifest of more than 8 MiB is an error: `Cargo manifest {path} is larger than 8 MiB` (code `remeris::workspace::too_large`), for the root and for a member. Only regular files are read (a symlink to one is fine): a FIFO, device or directory is `not a regular file`, without being opened. | A hostile repository must not exhaust memory or block discovery; reading a prefix would silently lose members or dependencies. |
| Members are joined literally: `{member}/Cargo.toml`, so `..` and absolute members leave the repository. | A member that is empty, absolute or has a `..` component is an error: `The Cargo workspace member {m} must be a path inside the workspace` (code `remeris::workspace::members`). Other members are cleaned like `path.Clean`: `./a` and `a/` read `a/Cargo.toml` (which is also the path in `versioned_files`), and `.` is the root manifest. Globs are not supported, as in Knope (`crates/*` fails to read `crates/*/Cargo.toml`). | A manifest from a pull request must not make a release read files outside the checkout. |
| `workspace` must be a standard table (`as_table`). | The same: `workspace = { members = [...] }` before the first table header and `[[workspace.members]]` are no workspace; a dotted `workspace.members = [...]` is one. A key called `workspace` inside another table is not looked at. The generic TOML decoder cannot tell inline tables from standard ones, so the source text is scanned for these forms. | Same result as Knope. |

### npm workspaces

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patterns that leave the project | An error, `Could not process workspaces glob pattern "{p}" in package.json: {reason}` (`remeris::workspaces::npm_glob`), as for a pattern that does not compile. The patterns refused are `..` components, absolute paths, NUL bytes and, on Windows, backslashes, colons (volumes, UNC paths, streams) and device names. Knope's glob crate accepts them. | Patterns cannot escape the project lexically. Symbolic links are followed as in Knope, so a link inside the project may still lead outside it (`versioned_files` can use `..` too). |
| Pattern in messages | The pattern is printed once, quoted with Go syntax, so control and ANSI characters from the repository do not reach the terminal. Knope prints it raw. | Safety of the terminal output. |
| A directory matched by several patterns | The package appears once, at its first position. Knope lists it once per match, which gives two packages with the same name. | A duplicate package would be released twice. |
| Manifest size and kind | A `package.json` of more than 8 MiB, the root one or a member's, is an error (code `remeris::workspace::too_large`); Knope reads it whole. A member `package.json` that is not a regular file (a FIFO, a device, a directory) is skipped like an unreadable one, because opening a FIFO would block. | Bounds the memory and never blocks on a file the configuration points at; a silent skip of a big file would drop packages. |
| Glob errors while walking | A directory that cannot be read is skipped (as in Knope); the other matches stay. | Parity. |

### Deno workspaces

Spec F20.4. Knope uses `deno_config` 0.97 (`WorkspaceDirectory::discover`); the notes below say where remeris differs.

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where the workspace is looked for | The working directory only. `deno_config` also walks up to a parent directory that holds a workspace whose members include the working directory; remeris does not, and a `knope.toml` in a member directory releases that member alone. | Discovery reads the working directory's file system only (`fs.StatFS` rooted there). |
| Root `package.json` `workspaces` | Not folded into the Deno workspace. Knope reads them through `deno_config` (`discover_pkg_json`), which makes the same packages appear twice when the npm detector also finds them. | The npm detector owns them. A root `package.json` is read here only for a root that has a `deno.json(c)`. |
| Order of the members | The root folder first, then the members sorted by their directory URL string with a trailing slash (`a-b/` before `a/`, because `-` sorts before `/`), whatever the order in `workspace`. `deno_config` keeps them in a `BTreeMap` keyed by URL. | Read from the source of 0.97, not tested against a Deno build; `config_folders()` is an `IndexMap` filled in that order. Characters that URLs percent-encode (spaces, non-ASCII) sort by their raw bytes here and by their encoded form in `deno_config`. Pinned by the `reversed declared order` and `members sorted by URL` tests. |
| Glob members | A member with `*` or `?` finds the directories under it that hold a `deno.json`, `deno.jsonc` or `package.json`; `[` and `]` are literal. As in `deno_config`, a `!pattern` excludes exactly the directories the pattern matches (never their subdirectories), a directory below a symbolic link is never a member (matches are dropped when a component of their directory is a link), and a component that starts with `.` is matched only by a pattern component that starts with a literal `.` (`packages/*` does not find `packages/.template`; `**` never enters a hidden directory). `.git` and `node_modules` directories are skipped. | `deno_config` collects files with lstat and `require_literal_leading_dot`. Not done: `internal/glob` has no options, so the walk itself still enters links and hidden or ignored directories and the matches are filtered afterwards (a link to `/` is still walked by the glob, only its matches are dropped); patterns are matched case sensitively where `deno_config` is not; how a negated pattern combines with the others in odd cases is not checked. |
| Duplicates | The same text twice is ignored, as in `deno_config` (a set of pairs); the same directory written two ways, or reached by a glob and by a path, is `Cannot specify a workspace member twice`. Two `deno.json(c)` with the same `name` are an error even when they have no `version`; `package.json` names are not compared. | Parity. |
| Errors | `Failed to discover Deno workspace: …` (code `remeris::workspace::deno_discover`), with the relative path where `deno_config` prints a `file://` URL, every member text, name, path and pattern quoted with `%q`, and without the file's content or the JSON library's text: a file that does not parse is `Could not parse "{path}"`, one nested deeper than 10000 levels `Could not parse "{path}": nesting is deeper than 10000 levels`, a file over 8 MiB `"{path}" is larger than 8 MiB` (code `remeris::workspace::too_large`), and a FIFO, device or directory `Could not read "{path}"`. A `package.json` that does not parse is an error too, but only in a workspace that has a root `deno.json(c)`. | Different libraries; the limits, `Could not read` and the no-content rule are ours (`hujson` recurses without a limit and would overflow the stack). |
| `workspace` shape | `null` or absent is no members; an array of strings or `{"members": […]}` (no other key) is accepted; anything else is `Failed to parse "workspace" configuration.` | Parity with `to_workspace_config`. |
| Lockfile | `lock` is `false` (none), `true`, a path, or an object (its `path`, else the default). The default is `deno.lock` next to the root config. It is used only if the file exists. A path that leaves the project (absolute, a drive or UNC path, a backslash on Windows, or starting with `..` after cleaning) is an error `Failed to resolve deno.lock path: … is outside the project directory` whether or not the file exists. A lock that exists but is not a regular file (a directory, FIFO or device, links followed) is an error too, since a release would write to it. Knope accepts a `..` path that exists and fails only on an absolute path outside the directory; a `lock` of another type is an error in both. | A release must not edit a file outside the project, or block on a FIFO (spec F20.4). |
| Import edges | The `jsr:` and `npm:` requirements are read from `imports`, every scope of `scopes` and `compilerOptions` (`jsxImportSource`, `jsxImportSourceTypes`, `types`), as `ConfigFile::dependencies` does. The name is found as `deno_semver` does (the path starts at the first `/`, or the second after a leading `@`; the requirement starts at the last `@` after the first character), so `jsr:foo@1` is a requirement on `foo` and `jsr:@/a` on `@/a`. The version requirement is not parsed, so `jsr:@a/b@nonsense` counts as a requirement on `@a/b`; Deno would not see one. | `pkg/versioning/internal/denosemver` cannot be imported from `internal/config`; only the name matters here. |
| Typed fields | As in `deno_config`, a `name` or `version` that is not a string (or null), and a `lock.path` that is not a string, make the file not parse (`Could not parse "{path}"`). A `deno.json(c)` that holds `null` is the default configuration. | Parity with serde. |
| Edges from `package.json` | Read from `dependencies` and `devDependencies` only, as `deno_package_json` 0.49 resolves them (strings and numbers; other values are dropped). The entry is parsed like `PackageJsonDepValue::parse`: `file:`, `jsr:`, `npm:`, `workspace:` or a plain requirement on the key, any other scheme is skipped. A requirement is skipped when it does not parse, and remeris checks that with its own reduction of the npm range grammar (`validNPMVersionReq`): a single range that is neither a valid tag nor a range of the grammar is skipped, `||` alternatives always parse, numbers are not range checked. `file:` paths are resolved logically against the dependent's directory below the project root and compared with the directory or config file of the released member; a path that climbs above the root or starts with `/` never matches, where Knope resolves against the absolute directory (so `../<root name>/b` would match there). A `npm:` value is cut at its last `@` without checking for a sub-path (`npm:b/sub` names `b/sub`, which matches nothing). The file listed is the dependent's config (its `deno.json(c)` when it has one), so a dependent with a `deno.json` is listed but its `package.json` is not edited by the release. | Port of `package_json_dep_matches`; no file system access, `internal/config` cannot import `pkg/versioning/internal/denosemver`. |
| Empty `name` | A `name` or `version` that is the empty string does not make a package. Knope accepts the empty name. | An empty package name cannot be released. |

## --validate

Audited against `main.rs` and `workflow.rs` of Knope: the mode runs every workflow as a dry run with the logs off, on a copy of the state each, collects one `Problem with workflow {name}` per failing workflow, in declaration order, under `There are problems with the defined workflows`, and exits 1. Configuration errors and package errors come first, `--override-version` and `--prerelease-label` are applied before the workflows run, and a dry run reads no credentials and prompts for nothing. These behave the same.

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--validate` (or `--upgrade`) without a `knope.toml` | Not a flag, as in Knope (`ConfigSource::Default` defines only `--generate`): `unexpected argument '--validate' found`, with the help `To pass '--validate' as a value, use '-- --validate'.`. Exit code 1; clap exits with 2 and prints a usage block. The same text is used for every unknown flag, of the root and of a workflow. | urfave/cli's own message (`flag provided but not defined: -validate`, plus a usage dump) is replaced by clap's wording. |
| An unknown workflow name with `--validate`, `--generate` or `--upgrade` | `No workflow named {name}`, before the mode runs. | clap rejects an unknown subcommand before it looks at any flag. Its text differs (`unrecognized subcommand`) and its exit code is 2. |
| Steps of milestone M11 (`SelectGitHubIssue`, `SelectGiteaIssue`, `SelectJiraIssue`, `TransitionJiraIssue`, `SwitchBranches`, `RebaseBranch`, `SelectIssueFromBranch`) | Fail in a dry run with `Step X is not implemented yet (milestone M11)`, so `--validate` reports a workflow that uses them even when Knope would pass it. | The steps have no implementation yet; passing them would hide that. `validate/kitchen_sink_issues` is skipped until they exist. |
| Exit code and rendering | Exit code 1 for every error. The related errors are printed as `╰─▶` lines by `internal/diag`, without miette's `Error:` blocks, codes and URLs. | Spec F3.3, D4. |

## M10 --generate and --upgrade

### Configuration document

`Config.Document()` maps the loaded configuration to the TOML that `--generate` and `--upgrade` write (spec F20.7, F21).

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[release_notes]` | Written when the configuration has it, with its `change_templates`. Knope's `SimpleConfig` has no such field, so `--upgrade` silently drops a user's templates. | Rewriting the file must not lose settings. |
| `[jira]` | Written when set, after `[gitea]`. Knope's `SimpleConfig` drops it. | Same. |
| `[github]` `api_url`, `upload_url` | Written when set (remeris keys; Knope has no slot for them). | Same. |
| `shell = false` | Left out. Knope stores `Option<bool>` and keeps an explicit `false`; the configuration here is a `bool`, which cannot tell it from no key. The two run the same way. | The step model has no tri-state. |
| `ignore_conventional_merge_commits` | Not written: `[changes]` has no such key in remeris yet. Knope writes it (and `[changes]`) when it is true. Add it here when the key is added to the model. | Gap in the configuration model. |
| Template `variables` | A `CreatePullRequest` title or body without a `variables` key is written with the default variables (`"$version" = "Version"`, `"$changelog" = "ChangelogEntry"`), as Knope does. A `Command` without `variables` stays without. | Knope's `Template` always holds a map; loaded again, both mean the same. |
| One named package | Written as `[packages.<name>]`; `[package]` is only for the unnamed default package. Knope writes a lone package as `[package]` whatever its name, so it loads back as the default package: its release tags change from `name/vX` to `vX`, the next changelog takes the whole history and `Release` tags `vX`. With two or more packages, the default package is called `default`. | The document must keep the tag identity of the package. |
| An all-table `versioned_files` | Written as `[[package.versioned_files]]` sections, not inline tables, because the toml crate prints an array of only tables that way (no Knope golden covers it; `internal/tomlwrite` implements the rule). | Byte parity with `toml::to_string`. |

### --generate

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing path | `remeris --generate` fails with `knope.toml already exists` (help: `Remove or rename it to generate a new one. remeris never overwrites a configuration file.`, code `remeris::generate::exists`, exit 1) whenever the path exists: a file that cannot be read, a directory, a symbolic link (dangling or not, never followed). Knope overwrites the path whenever reading it failed, for any reason. A knope.toml that can be read (even an invalid one) removes the flag, as in Knope. | `--generate` must not destroy a file the user did not mean to lose. The file is created exclusively and atomically (`fsx.WriteNew`: temporary file, then hard link; exclusive create where links are unsupported), so a concurrent file is never replaced either. |
| `--dry-run` | Writes nothing. Prints `Would generate a knope.toml file:` and then the file, to stdout (no `Generating a knope.toml file` line), or the same `already exists` error when the path is taken. Knope ignores `--dry-run` here and writes the file. | A dry run must not change the repository (spec F3.1). |
| Order | A package discovery error is reported first, before any log line, in a real and a dry run. | Knope reports it while loading the configuration. |
| Mode | The file is created with mode `0666` before the umask, as Knope's `fs::write`. | Parity. |

### --upgrade

`remeris --upgrade` moves `ignore_conventional_commits` from the `PrepareRelease` steps to `[changes]` and regenerates `knope.toml` from `Config.Document()` (Quirk Q9).

| Case | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warning | After a real upgrade remeris prints one line: `Warning: knope.toml was regenerated: its comments and formatting were not kept.` Knope prints nothing. | The file is regenerated (Q9); the user should know before committing. |
| `--dry-run` | Writes nothing and prints `Would upgrade knope.toml:` followed by the TOML that would be written, or `Nothing to upgrade`. Knope ignores `--dry-run` here and writes the file. | A dry run must not touch disk. |
| Nothing to upgrade | The file is not rewritten, not even with identical bytes. | Same as Knope's behaviour in practice; tested byte for byte. |
| Atomic write | The new file is written to a temporary file in the same directory (mode of the original), synced, and renamed over `knope.toml`; any failure leaves `knope.toml` untouched and removes the temporary file. An empty result for a non-empty file is refused. Knope calls `fs::write`. | An interrupted write must not destroy the configuration. |
| Symbolic link | A `knope.toml` that is a symbolic link is refused: `knope.toml is a symbolic link, so it was not changed`, with the help `Replace the link by the file, or edit the file it points to.` (code `remeris::upgrade::symlink`). Knope writes through the link. | The link is never followed or replaced. |
| Prerelease label | `--upgrade` runs on the configuration before `--prerelease-label` (or `REMERIS_PRERELEASE_LABEL`, `KNOPE_PRERELEASE_LABEL`) is applied, so the label never reaches the file. `--generate` is the same. | Knope upgrades first too; the order is fixed in `workflowCommand`. |
| Dropped settings | Knope's `SimpleConfig` drops `[jira]`, `[release_notes]` and the `api_url`/`upload_url` of `[github]`; remeris keeps them (see the configuration document above). | Rewriting the file must not lose settings. |
| Discovery error | A deferred package discovery error is reported before anything is written. | The discovered packages are written out, so they must be known. |
| One named package | A lone `[packages.foo]` stays `[packages.foo]` (see the configuration document above), so its tag history is kept. | Parity with the document, not with Knope's `write_out`. |
| Unknown keys | A file with a key remeris does not read (`[changes] ignore_conventional_merge_commits`, a typo, a key of a newer Knope) is refused when a rewrite is needed: `knope.toml has keys that --upgrade would drop: …` (code `remeris::upgrade::unknown_key`), nothing is written, also in a dry run. A file with nothing to upgrade is never refused. Knope drops what its `SimpleConfig` does not model. | The loader ignores unknown keys (Q1); the rewrite must not lose them silently. |
| Read-only file | A `knope.toml` without the owner write bit is refused (`knope.toml is read-only, so it was not changed`, code `remeris::upgrade::read_only`). A rename would replace it silently; Knope's `fs::write` fails with `EACCES`. | Same outcome as Knope. |
| Not preserved | Only the permission bits are copied (not setuid, setgid or sticky); ACLs and extended attributes are lost; a hard link to the file keeps the old content; a read-only target on Windows is refused only if the attribute maps to the mode. The owner and group are restored on Unix when the process may (errors ignored, not tested). A crash between creating the temporary file and the rename leaves `.knope.toml.*.tmp` in the directory (untracked in Git). | Consequences of replacing the file instead of writing into it. |
| Frozen at upgrade time | The forge detected from the remote and, in a hybrid file, the discovered packages are written into the file, so a later change of layout needs a manual edit. `--upgrade` never writes the default workflows: a file with no `PrepareRelease` flag to move is `Nothing to upgrade`. | Quirk Q9. |
